title: Etale source inverse image preserves universal coefficient arrows
statement: Let Z be a scheme, q:R→S a homomorphism of commutative rings in Type(u+1), C a derived R-module sheaf and Cprime a derived S-module sheaf on Z_et. Suppose δ:C→Res_q(Cprime) is initial as a structured arrow for derived scalar restriction [def-weil-pbc-derived-normalization-arrows]. For every V in Z_et, the specified etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow Z q δ V [def-weil-pbc-etale-isomorphism-normalization-arrow] is initial for derived scalar restriction on V_et. Neither boundedness nor flatness of S over R is assumed. This is a preservation statement, with no comparison site, adic tower, realization or descent equation.

source.place: Tags 06YS (K-flat resolutions), 0G7E (pullback preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms), and 0D6D (composition of derived pullbacks). Also proetale.tex Tag 09B1 for exact conservative comparison, or the small etale site Tag 03ED for etale source restriction, respectively.

proof.text: Use the ordinary scalar-extension adjunctions and their normalized derived adjunction data from WitnessCompatibility. The canonical normalizationPullbackIso is defined as the inverse geometric mate of the sectionwise identity; applying the geometric mate again therefore gives the identity by Equiv.apply_symm_apply. The iterated-mates criterion makes its ordinary scalar-extension mate invertible. Etale inverse image preserves flat sheaves by the geometric-fiber criterion. Apply the proved generic derived_mate_isIso_of_flat to this very comparison and the normalized scalar adjunctions. The mapDerivedCategoryNatIso symmetry identity identifies its conclusion with the inverse scalar mate of the canonical localized normalizationPullbackIso.

For arbitrary adjunctions and a square with invertible inverse mate, identify a universal structured arrow with the first adjunction unit followed by a unique target isomorphism, using mkInitialOfLeftAdjoint.uniqueUpToIso. Compose the component of the invertible mate with the image of that target isomorphism. unit_mateEquiv_symm and naturality show that the second adjunction unit followed by this isomorphism equals precisely the pulled original arrow followed by the specified coefficient square. StructuredArrow.isoMk and preservation of initiality under isomorphism prove universality. Instantiate with exact etale inverse image, normalized scalar adjunctions, and the coefficient comparison of etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow. This imposes no boundedness, flat coefficient map, or nonempty-source assumption.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YS, 0G7E and 0D6D; direct use of the proved generic flat-resolution mate comparison and normalized derived scalar adjunctions in Sheaf.Paper.WitnessCompatibility, together with the source-library etale flat-pullback instance and Mathlib adjunction-mate/initial-object identities.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleSourceNormalization_universal (Z : Scheme.{u})
    {R S : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (q : R →+* S)
    {C : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R))}
    {C' : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} S))}
    (δ : C ⟶ (normalizationRestrict Z.smallEtaleTopology q).obj C')
    (h : Nonempty (StructuredArrow.IsUniversal
      (StructuredArrow.mk δ : StructuredArrow _
        (normalizationRestrict Z.smallEtaleTopology q))))
    (V : Z.Etale) :
    Nonempty (StructuredArrow.IsUniversal (StructuredArrow.mk
      (etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow Z q δ V)))
